gaps.lead: My advice is to check the contract twice before signing.
gaps.sentence: You ___ the contract twice before signing.
gaps.explanation: had better + infinitive without 'to' = strong advice.

gaps.lead: The garage is servicing my car tomorrow morning.
gaps.explanation: Arranged service: have/get something done — having my car serviced.

gaps.lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
gaps.explanation: should(n't) have + participle criticises a past decision.

gaps.lead: Do you mind if I come over to see you later?
gaps.sentence: Do you ___ coming over to see you later?
gaps.explanation: 'Have any objection to me/my coming' is the formal equivalent of 'do you mind'.

gaps.lead: 'I'm sorry I was so rude to your sister,' Maria said.
gaps.sentence: Maria apologised ___ so rude to my sister.
gaps.explanation: apologise for + -ing: apologised for being so rude.
